WHAT DOES THIS TOOL LOOK FOR?

How we measure flashing under WCAG 2.2

1. Flash Speed (Frequency)

The 3-Flash Rule: Under WCAG SC 2.3.1, content must not flash more than 3 times in any 1-second period.

A "flash" requires two opposing brightness transitions (e.g. dark → light → dark is one complete flash). 4 or more flashes in 1 second is dangerous.

2. Relative Luminance (Brightness)

Contrast Threshold: Not all flashing is hazardous. To count as a general flash, the brightness jump must be at least 10% (ΔY ≥ 0.10) and the darker state must be below 80% brightness.

Y = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B

This calculates how human eyes perceive brightness across red, green, and blue light.

3. Saturated Red Flashes

Red Transitions: Rapid transitions to or from bright saturated red are especially hazardous and can trigger seizures even when overall brightness changes are smaller.

The detector monitors both general brightness flashes and chromaticity changes toward pure red.

WCAG 2.2 COMPLIANCE CONTEXT

Evidence for human review.
Never an automated "pass."

Accessibility standards require that web pages and applications do not contain flashing content that can harm photosensitive users. This tool gathers forensic timing and luminance data to help auditors make informed decisions.

Because video compression, display refresh rates, and viewing distance vary, no software can issue an automatic legal compliance certificate. Always verify flagged timestamps with a qualified accessibility specialist.

What can automated browser screening miss?

High-frequency strobes above 60 Hz, subtle color shifts, moving camera pans with repetitive textures (like picket fences or escalators), or protected DRM video streams that browser tab capture cannot read.
